front: When did the Berlin Blockade begin and end?

back: Supplying a place by air; used to feed and fuel West Berlin in 1948-49.

front: When were NATO and the Warsaw Pact formed?
When were the two German states set up?
back: 1949: Federal Republic (West) in May; German Democratic Republic (East) in October.

front: Why did Stalin blockade West Berlin?
back: To stop a separate West German state (new Deutschmark) and to force the West out of Berlin.

front: Why was the airlift a Western success?
back: West Berlin survived; Stalin backed down without war, and the USA showed it would defend allies.

front: Revisionist view of the Cold War
back: The view (influential from the 1960s) that the USA, with its economic and atomic power, was mainly to blame.

front: Post-revisionist view of the Cold War
back: The view that both superpowers share the blame through mutual fear and misunderstanding.

front: What does the traditional view say about the Cold War?
back: The USSR was to blame: it broke the Yalta promise and imposed communism on Eastern Europe; the USA only reacted.
